title: Thane Heins coil reverses generator drag, replicated by Gary

tellings.quote: when I put his coil on, which has higher inductance, when you tell that coil to power a load, the rotation speed increases and the input current goes down.

plain: A coil designed by a Canadian inventor named Thane Heins is said to reverse the usual drag on a generator. Normally a generator slows when it powers something, but the British computer hacker Gary McKinnon tells Michels that when he fitted Heins's coil, which has higher inductance, and set it to power a load, "the rotation speed increases and the input current goes down." McKinnon says he got this result himself in the UK; if it held up, a generator would get easier to run as it does work.
